column1: # load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie: the logos and the opening are movies)
# Unreal Engine 4.2x: nninitStartup needs virtual address memory and reserves one address region for the engine, 62 GB by default. This build reserves it only when
# -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize= is absent (main+0x1aa9b64: ldr of the size variable, cbz to the 62 GB default and nn::os::AllocateAddressRegion at main+0x1aa9d44), as Pikmin 4's:
# with the option the region's base stayed 0 and the first commit, AllocateMemoryPages(0 + offset) (main+0x1aaa9e0), failed with 0x7 into Unreal's LowLevelFatalError (line 919), so no
# game_args. The rewriter's engine-wide gate on the store of its size (dm/tools/ue_region.py, the store at main+0x1aa9d40) gives it what the alias region has room for. Its allocator,
# an FMallocBinned3 made on the first allocation (GCreateMalloc, main+0x1aaa350), would cut 37 GB of pools out of that region; the constructor call (main+0x1aaa368) is cut and the
# host runs Unreal's heap on a malloc zone outside the guest block (the rewriter's engine-wide cut, dm/tools/ue_malloc.py; hle_uemalloc.c layout UE4_24, the name getter at slot 17).
# The region sits in Engage's 5 GB block (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region), as Pikmin 4's and FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE's.
# Application pool 2 GB: Unreal sizes its page cache from the pool QueryMemoryInfo reports (1.87 GB of a 2 GB pool), and the iPhone run that played was made with it
# the NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the host writes t.MaxFPS 60 and rhi.SyncInterval 1 into its console variables, which the rewriter finds by name (dm/tools/ue_cvar.py: t.MaxFPS at
# main+0x88177d8, rhi.SyncInterval at main+0x871f080), so the game asks for present interval 1 itself. Unreal steps the game by the time that really passed. The player's Frame rate
# (or DM_FPS_TARGET=30 in Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) keeps the game's 30 and saves power
